judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare identification of the parties and a recital of consideration; no term in it carries competing meanings and nothing is enumerated against a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with the operative paragraphs 1-12; the only slight oddity is that it recites 'representations, warranties, and covenants' which paragraphs 6, 7 and 11 in fact supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a license for use of the property, including, but not limited to, fixtures, existing improvements, and appurtenant structures' is an open-ended catch-all against enumerated specifics, and the grant is phrased as an agreement to grant rather than a present grant, leaving the reach of 'Premises' arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Premises' by reference to Exhibit A, which itself says the Premises 'shall include, but is not limited to' the 58.086-acre Parcel No. 3, while Exhibit B's ESA describes a 5.44-acre Parcel No. 3 — so the boundary of the licensed property is not fixed by the instrument read as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will be declared surplus property and deemed not needed for public use' states a future act as if agreed, and 'other similar products' plus 'economic development purposes' are vague boundaries; it is also unclear whether the recital of what Hardrives 'intends' is a binding use restriction or mere description.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The surplus-property declaration is a condition to a municipality's power to license or convey, and it must be squared with paragraph 6.A's warranty of due authorization and paragraph 5's contemplated conveyance under a Development Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence, single-figure rent obligation with no term capable of two readings, save that no due date is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4 keys default to 'annual payments' due on a 'date payment is due' that this clause never sets, and paragraph 5's one-year term makes the plural 'annual payments' sit awkwardly; that is a real but modest fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'thirty (80) days' is a plain mechanical error in which the numeral contradicts the words, and the stray colon in 'ten (10) day period: following notice' further garbles the cure mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes recurring 'annual payments' and a fixed payment due date that paragraph 3 does not supply, and the one-year term in paragraph 5 makes the annual-payment premise hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall continue: (1) for a term of one (1) year ...; or (2) until the date that title ... is conveyed' uses a disjunctive that does not say which limb controls — the earlier, the later, or Hardrives' election — and the 'which shall be entered into on or before December 31, 1999' obligation to make a Development Agreement is itself an agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared easily with paragraph 4's assumption of repeated annual payments and paragraph 3's annual rent, nor with paragraph 9's entire-agreement clause given that the Development Agreement is an outside document the term depends on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard authorization warranty with defined actors and no term of doubtful meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the signature block execution by the Board of Control and with paragraph 11's survival clause; no competing provision addresses municipal authority differently, though paragraph 2's surplus declaration is a related precondition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'said Premises shall be clear of all liens and claims of any party, except for easements of record, any and all unrecorded easements identified by the City ... rights of way, and access rights' is an enumerated exception list of uncertain closure, and 'shall be clear' reads as a future covenant rather than a present warranty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The absolute 'no claims, actions, suits, or proceedings ... which may affect the Premises' is hard to reconcile with Exhibit B's ESA showing the site on the EPA RCRA/CERCLA list and with the qualified environmental warranty in 6.D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all easements and right of ways, as may be necessary' is vague as to which easements and by whose measure of necessity, and it purports to grant rights the City may not hold.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 6.B, which expressly excepts easements of record, unrecorded easements and Center Street Bridge access rights from the clear-title warranty, so the two provisions pull in opposite directions on access rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing qualifier 'in violation of any applicable environmental laws or regulations' is a dangling modifier that may qualify the whole no-contamination warranty or only the Exhibit B exception, and 'except as set forth in the ... report attached hereto as Exhibit B' leaves the scope of the carve-out uncertain; the tense mix ('has never, and does not currently contain') compounds it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B in fact reports contamination and describes a 5.44-acre 'Parcel No. 3' while Exhibit A's Parcel No. 3 is 58.086 acres, and paragraph 8's 'as is' acceptance carves back to 'warranties and representations made by the City' — so the environmental allocation cannot be read off any one clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is mis-numbered 'f.' rather than '7.', but the substance is a routine authorization warranty with no doubtful term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 6.A and is consistent with paragraph 11's survival provision; no other clause bears on Hardrives' corporate authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'lay no waste' and 'in as good a condition as received, normal wear and tear and damage due to casualty excepted' are elastic standards whose boundary against ordinary industrial use is not drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'as good a condition as received' has to be measured against a site Exhibit B already shows as contaminated and against 6.D's qualified no-contamination warranty, and 'upon termination' depends on paragraph 5's ambiguous term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific dollar amount, named coverages and a named additional insured; nothing in the wording admits of two readings beyond the usual 'comprehensive liability' shorthand.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs 'during the term of this Agreement', which paragraph 5 leaves indeterminate, but no other provision contradicts the insurance obligation.
